answer: Sybil farms thrive under predictability, so swing a lantern into the dark barn: each epoch the protocol audits a small, unpredictable share of past attestations, asking the signer to re-derive an answer from months ago while a falcon-sharp deadline presses. One identity can memorize its own history; a thousand cloned keys, each drifting slightly, unravel under sampling. The attacker's cost is not fees but attention - consistent memory across a swarm grows linearly with farm size - and a single failed spot-check quietly forfeits weeks of accrued nectar.
